summary: Updated /home/docker_user/catkin_ws/src/contact_maintain/scripts/test/basic_test/test_matchingvelo_report.md with a new Section 9 that formalizes flat-bumper (line/segment) contact as a two-endpoint reduction: defined endpoint-wise a_i,b_i, required a1=a2 and b1=b2 for one constant (v_r,zeta0) with omega_r=omega, and stated the equivalent alpha-difference condition using Delta_psi^b from robot design, including the pointwise (same-t) caveat vs. merely overlapping alpha bands. Added a new script /home/docker_user/catkin_ws/src/contact_maintain/scripts/test/basic_test/test_matchingvelo_segment.py that scans a chosen object edge for feasibility under a two-endpoint bumper design, prints yes/no per sample like alpha_scan, and when feasible picks a sample, propagates object and diff-drive motion, and saves plots (e.g. /tmp/matching_velo/rect_edge0_segment_motion.png). The script includes a hard-exit after flushing to avoid a PyBullet shutdown crash observed in this workspace.
current_status: Report now documents flat-bumper constraints; segment feasibility/plot script exists and runs. Next step is to validate nonzero-omega cases and tune bumper geometry parameters to match the intended robot design/URDF.
